taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 0 state changes, each allowed by a review (0 reviews in all)
1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
I read all twelve codes in RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics, June 2022). The search turned up no newer HTTP Semantics RFC that obsoletes it. Section 15 says that among the codes in this specification, only 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414 and 501 are heuristically cacheable. All other codes are not. Each section I read matches that list. Every quote below comes from the code's own section of the page.

Two codes have reason phrases that differ from older RFCs: 413 is "Content Too Large" (RFC 7231 called it "Payload Too Large") and 422 is "Unprocessable Content". I used the RFC 9110 phrasing.

Heuristically cacheable: 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501. Not heuristically cacheable: 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422.

Source for everything: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
